relevance_note: This 36-child Vietnamese VEO-IBD cohort lists two patients (P22/G1, P23/G1) with TNFAIP3 monogenic findings in Table 3: "patients with TNFAIP3 (A20 haploinsufficiency) variants (n = 2)".
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I transcribed by hand from Table 3 (patients as rows) and the text, then checked every span verbatim against the paper and every field against the schema. Scope: Table 3 gives patient-level data for 24 cohort patients, but only P22/G1 and P23/G1 carry TNFAIP3 findings; the 22 patients with variants in other genes (TTC7A, MYO5B, XIAP, CYBB, MEFV, MCM10, FOXP3, IL10RB, IL10RA, IRGM) were not extracted, because this is an HA20 curation study. Reverse this if all cohort rows are wanted. Relatives: the sibling of P23/G1 ('Sibling died from EBV-HLH.' in P23/G1's row) is a separate row labelled 'Sibling'. The paper gives no family labels, so the link to P23/G1 appears only in the spans. Both TNFAIP3 patients have FH = 'Yes' (first-degree relative with IBD), but those relatives are not otherwise described (number and relationship unknown), so no rows were created for them. Whether the P23 sibling is that relative is not stated. Variants: the paper prints no TNFAIP3 variant description, transcript or zygosity. They are in Supplementary Table S2, which is not in the full text. Each TNFAIP3 patient therefore has one variants row with variant_original_string 'not reported'. The pathogenicity value is the Table 3 group 'G1: Monogenic findings', which the Methods define as P/LP under ACMG. Zygosity was not inferred from the label 'haploinsufficiency'. Ages: T1/T2 are in months per the Table 3 notes ('T1: Age at symptom onset (months)', 'T2: Age at diagnosis (months)'). Ethnicity 'Vietnamese' and the diagnosis basis come from cohort-level statements (abstract and Methods) applied to each cohort patient. is_proband is null for P22/G1 and P23/G1: they are cohort patients the paper never calls probands. Fever: both patients have 'persistent fever'. Checklist 'recurrent fever' was left 'not reported' because persistent is not the same as recurrent; the fever is kept as a phenotypic_features row. Group statement in the Discussion (HA20 patients 'including recurrent bloody diarrhea, persistent fever, oral ulcers, arthritis, dermatitis, and growth failure') is a union across the two patients: oral ulcers appear only in P22's row, and dermatitis and growth failure only in P23's. It was not used to attribute features to either patient, so it is not treated as a contradiction. Minor inconsistencies in the paper: the Table 3 column is 'FH' but the note defines 'HF'; the Methods data statement ('available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request') contradicts the end-matter one ('contained within the article and Supplementary Materials'). No contradictions about the TNFAIP3 patients' features.
